newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Social partners close to deal on part-time work.
newsitem.headline: Social partners close to deal on part-time work.

text.p: The "big three" European Union labour and management groups are close to an agreement on rules to guarantee rights to part-time workers, the head of the European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) said on Wednesday.
"We're very close to a positive result if the last remaining obstacles can be lifted," ETUC secretary general Emilio Gabaglio told a news conference.
The industry federation UNICE, the public employers group CEEP and the ETUC have already sketched out a draft compromise which will be the subject of a final round of negotiations on May 14.
If the talks succeed, the deal will be formally approved by the three groups at a meeting in Brussels on June 5-6.
Both unions and employers declined to comment on the details of the draft compromise and on the obstacles which might still block a deal.
"The employers need to understand that flexibility must be balanced by greater security for workers," Gabaglio said.

But a UNICE spokeswoman told Reuters there was a need for job arrangements to be more flexible and the unions had to understand that job security did not mean ruling out any alteration in workers' acquired rights.

The three groups agreed last June to open talks on rights for part-time workers after the European Commission asked them to consider ways of ensuring that employees in a broad range of flexible jobs did not face discrimination.
The Maastricht Treaty's social protocol gives these groups -- the so-called social partners -- the right to strike a deal and then ask the EU Council of Ministers to turn it into EU law.
At UNICE's insistence, the negotiations have been confined solely to part-time work and have not covered other types of flexible jobs such as fixed-term or temporary contracts.

A spokesman for ETUC said the unions had accepted this constriction in order to get a rapid deal on part-time workers but they would continue to press for better rights for people doing other atypical forms of work.
